note: Synthetic test scenarios only. Not real patient data. Used to validate the safety-check and service-finder logic end-to-end.

scenarios.label: emergency_chest_pain
scenarios.user_text: My dad is clutching his chest and saying it feels like something is crushing him. He's sweating a lot and his left arm hurts. This started about 10 minutes ago.
scenarios.notes: Chest pain + radiation — must never reach service search; show emergency message immediately.

scenarios.label: emergency_stroke
scenarios.user_text: My mum's face is drooping on one side and her speech is slurred. She can't lift her right arm properly. It came on really suddenly about five minutes ago.
scenarios.notes: Classic FAST stroke signs — emergency path only.

scenarios.label: emergency_anaphylaxis
scenarios.user_text: I ate a peanut by accident and now my throat is swelling and I'm having trouble swallowing. I feel dizzy. I have an EpiPen but I'm scared to use it.
scenarios.notes: Anaphylaxis — throat swelling and difficulty swallowing are emergency markers.

scenarios.label: emergency_pregnancy
scenarios.user_text: I'm 32 weeks pregnant and I've started bleeding quite heavily. I also have a really bad headache and my vision is blurry.
scenarios.notes: Pregnant and bleeding heavily — emergency regardless of other context.

scenarios.label: urgent_self_harm_thoughts
scenarios.user_text: I've been having thoughts of hurting myself lately. I haven't done anything but the thoughts are getting louder and I don't know who to talk to.
scenarios.notes: Self-harm ideation — urgent tier, route to mental health specialist.

scenarios.label: urgent_fever_confusion
scenarios.user_text: My partner has a very high temperature — I think around 39.5 — and he's confused and not making much sense. This has been going on for about two hours.
scenarios.notes: High fever with confusion — urgent, likely same-day care at walk-in or A&E.

scenarios.label: urgent_child_ear_pain
scenarios.user_text: My 4-year-old has been crying all day with ear pain, she has a temperature of 38.5 and she keeps pulling at her ear. She hasn't slept.
scenarios.notes: Acute otitis media signs in a young child — urgent but not emergency; same-day GP.

scenarios.label: urgent_asthma_worsening
scenarios.user_text: I have asthma and my inhaler isn't helping as much today. I've used it five times already and I'm still quite breathless when I walk across the room.
scenarios.notes: Poor response to reliever inhaler — urgent, not yet full respiratory distress but needs same-day care.

scenarios.label: routine_repeat_prescription
scenarios.user_text: I need to request a repeat prescription for my blood pressure tablets. I have about a week's supply left.
scenarios.notes: Straightforward repeat prescription — routine, route to pharmacy or GP.

scenarios.label: routine_skin_rash
scenarios.user_text: I've had a mild itchy rash on my forearm for about a week. It's not spreading and I don't have a temperature. It might be a reaction to my new washing powder.
scenarios.notes: Mild, stable rash — routine GP appointment appropriate.

scenarios.label: routine_travel_vaccines
scenarios.user_text: I'm travelling to Southeast Asia in six weeks and I want to check which vaccinations I need. I haven't had any travel jabs before.
scenarios.notes: Travel health — routine, pharmacy travel clinic or GP nurse.

scenarios.label: routine_mental_health_support
scenarios.user_text: I've been feeling quite low and anxious for the past few weeks. It's affecting my sleep and my motivation at work. I'm not in crisis but I'd like some support.
scenarios.notes: Low mood and anxiety without crisis indicators — routine, route to IAPT/mental health specialist.
